_note: Padel IQ framework v0.1 (placeholder). Descriptors marked source=richard came from Richard; source=draft are first guesses for coaches to correct. Self-check quiz questions will live in a separate file and point to skill ids.

axes.name: Movement
axes.short: Position, recovery, moving as a pair

levels.name: Beginner
levels.description: Learning the rules and the court. Getting the ball over the net is the main challenge.
levels.coachFocus: Learn the rules and where to stand. Get the serve in and the ball over the net.

levels.name: D
levels.description: Consistent basics: you return reliably, serve in, and keep a simple rally going.
levels.coachFocus: Get it back. Keep the ball in play. No need for winners.

levels.name: C
levels.description: Controlled shots in friendly games: lobs, bandeja, basic glass play.
levels.coachFocus: Be consistent, and start aiming for spaces: the sides and the middle.

levels.name: B
levels.description: Reliable in matches: wins points on purpose, handles pressure.
levels.coachFocus: Build points on purpose: use depth, pace and height to move opponents, then finish when the ball is there.

levels.name: A
levels.description: Complete player: varied shots, smart tactics, and stays strong against good opponents.
levels.coachFocus: Control the match: vary spin and pace, read the opponents and change the plan when needed.

levels.name: Pro
levels.description: Professional level. The top benchmark, not an assessment target for most players.

rules._note: Draft rules from design chats. Not final.

levelPass.note: OPEN: all items, or most (placeholder 4 out of 5, no big gaps).

rules.axisLevel: Highest level whose master skills the player passes, worked out per axis.
rules.overallLevel: OPEN: not decided. Simple option: where most axes sit. Shown smaller than the pentagon.
rules.pushingAhead: A skill is 'pushing ahead' when the player's level is below the skill's first master level. It never raises or lowers their level.
rules.unratedSkills: Skills not yet rated are excluded from the calculation. They are not counted as D.
rules.plusLevels: OPEN: 'D+' could mean passed D and working through the C list. No minus levels.

journalPrompts: One thing to try next match?

statementCheck.rule: A player has a level for a skill when they are good enough at that level's statements (about 3 in 4 'usually' or 'always') AND have mastered every level below it (about 3 in 4 'always').
statementCheck.note: Agreed with Richard 26 Oct: mastery = always, good enough = usually. The 3-in-4 share is a placeholder.

beginner.text: Learning the serve. Often faults. Just trying to get it in the box.

D.text: In the right box about 7 or 8 out of 10. Soft and floaty. Not deep, no slice, no aiming at the side glass. The goal is just getting it in.

C.text: Usually in, with some depth. Can aim to a side or the body. Less reliable under pressure.

B.text: Reliable first serve with pace or slice. Placement is chosen on purpose and holds up when the score is tight.

A.text: Varies pace, spin and direction to set up the next shot. Targets weaknesses on purpose.

statements.text: I know how to serve: bounce, hit below the waist, diagonally into the box.
My serve goes in.
I can serve deep, close to the back glass.
I can aim my serve at the side glass or the body.
My first serve rarely misses, even at tight scores.
I can add pace without missing.
I can slice it so it stays low off the glass.
I choose the serve to suit the returner.
I mix pace, spin and direction so the returner can't settle.

D.text: Gets some easy lobs back with an overhead, mostly pushing the ball rather than hitting through it.

C.text: Gets under most lobs and hits a controlled overhead back, usually deep.

statements.text: I can get under easy lobs.
I can hit an overhead back over the net.
My overhead goes back deep and controlled.
I turn sideways and move back for lobs.

C.text: Can hit a bandeja in a friendly game to hold the net. Depth and direction vary.

B.text: Reliable bandeja that keeps opponents back and holds the net, even when rushed.

A.text: Chooses between attacking and defensive bandeja depending on the situation.

statements.text: I can hit a bandeja in a friendly game.
After my bandeja, I stay at the net.
My bandeja lands deep, so opponents stay back.
I can hit it when I'm rushed or moving back.
I can choose cross-court or straight.
I choose an attacking or a defensive bandeja depending on the ball.
I control slice and pace so it stays low off the glass.

B.text: Can use a víbora to add pace and angle when the ball is right for it.

A.text: Chooses víbora versus bandeja on purpose and places it under pressure.

statements.text: I can hit a víbora with side spin.
My víbora lands low into the side glass.
I choose víbora or bandeja depending on the lob.
I hit it hard without losing control, even under pressure.

B.text: Can attack a ball coming off the back glass with control.

A.text: Uses the bajada to finish points with placement and power.

statements.text: I attack balls that come off the back glass high.
I wait for the right height before hitting.
I place my bajada low, to the feet or down the middle.
I use the bajada to win the net back.

beginner.text: Gets some serves back, but often misses or hits it out.

D.text: Gets the ball over the net. Soft and floaty. Backhand is weaker.

C.text: Usually a safe, deep return. Backhand is steadier. Starts choosing direction.

B.text: Reliable return under pressure. Can choose a low, a lob or an attacking return.

A.text: Returns on purpose to win the net and hurts weak serves.

statements.text: I know where to stand to return.
I get most serves back.
My return goes low or to the middle.
I can return serves that come off the side glass.
I aim my return on purpose: low cross-court, middle or lob.
I return well, even at tight scores.
I choose the return to suit the server and their partner.
My return puts us on the attack.

D.text: Can get the lob over the net sometimes, but it's often too low or too short. Only works in an easy rally with plenty of time.

C.text: Usually gets a lob over in a friendly game when there is time. Height and depth are hit or miss. Falls apart when rushed or off the glass.

B.text: Usually lands a deep lob in matches, even when rushed. Pushes opponents back and lets you win the net. Mostly holds when the score is tight.

A.text: Chooses the lob on purpose: side, height, depth. Works from awkward positions and at big points against strong opponents.

statements.text: I can lob the ball over the net players.
My lob goes high and deep, not short.
After a good lob, I move up to the net.
I can lob from difficult spots, like off the glass or from the corner.
I aim my lob over the weaker overhead player, or down the middle.
I lob on purpose to win the net back, even under pressure.

D.text: Rarely plays off the glass, and often doesn't succeed when it does.

C.text: Can return most slow or medium balls off the back glass. Struggles with fast or awkward rebounds.

B.text: Reads rebounds early and returns most balls off the back glass with control.

A.text: Uses the glass to buy time and turn defence into attack.

statements.text: I let some balls hit the back glass before I play them.
I get easy rebounds back over the net.
I return most slow and medium rebounds.
I stand at the right distance from the glass.
I read fast rebounds early and return them with control.
After the glass, I can choose a lob or a low ball.
I use the glass to buy time and turn defence into attack.

C.text: Can return simple balls off the side glass. Often late on faster ones.

B.text: Reads side-glass angles and returns with control most of the time.

A.text: Handles fast and awkward side glass angles under pressure, and places the return.

statements.text: I return simple balls off the side glass.
I read the angle off the side glass early.
I return side glass balls with control most of the time.
I handle fast, awkward side glass balls under pressure, and place the return.

D.text: Knows the ready position and uses it on slow balls, but is often late on fast ones.

C.text: Usually ready before the opponent hits. Split step is inconsistent.

statements.text: I stand in a ready position between shots.
I'm ready before slow balls arrive.
I'm ready before the opponent hits.
I do a small split step as they hit.

D.text: Nothing consistent yet. Sometimes ends up at the net at the wrong time, or stays at the net all the time. Volleys are often a block that goes into the net or too high.

C.text: Takes the net when the chance is clear and holds it with steady volleys.

B.text: Wins and holds the net on purpose. Volleys have direction, attacking or defensive as needed.

A.text: Dominates the net. Redirects, finishes and recovers position quickly.

statements.text: I sometimes play at the net.
I take the net when the chance is clear.
Once I'm there, I stay with steady volleys.
I leave the net when we're in trouble, instead of staying there.
I win the net back on purpose, for example after a good lob.
I hold the net under pressure.
We control most points from the net.
I get back into my net position quickly after each shot.

C.text: Sometimes gets back into position after a shot. Often caught out of place.

B.text: Usually recovers to a good position before the next ball.

A.text: Recovers automatically, even after being pulled wide.

statements.text: After each shot, I move back into position.
I recover quickly after being pulled wide.
I move straight after hitting, instead of watching my shot.
I'm balanced and ready for the next ball, even in long rallies.

C.text: Aware of partner, but often both end up in the same spot or leave gaps.

B.text: Moves forward and back with partner most of the time.

A.text: Moves as one unit and covers the middle without thinking.

statements.text: My partner and I move forward together.
We move back together.
We move sideways together and keep the gap small.
We rarely go for the same ball.
We move as one, even when we switch sides.

D.text: Mostly just returns the ball. Knows the scoring but not yet when to attack or defend.

C.text: Starts to choose between safe and attacking shots. Often tries too much too soon.

B.text: Usually picks the right shot for the situation.

A.text: Chooses shots to set up the next one and targets weaknesses.

statements.text: When I'm in trouble, I just get the ball back safely.
I look at where the opponents are before I choose.
I choose placement over power.
I play the safe shot when I'm out of position.
I only go for winners when the ball is right.
I plan a few shots ahead.

C.text: Calls 'mine' or 'leave' sometimes. Middle balls often cause confusion.

B.text: Clear calls and agreed roles, including the middle.

A.text: Adjusts tactics with partner during the match.

statements.text: We call "mine", "yours" and "leave".
We agree who takes the middle.
We agree a simple plan before we start.
We talk between points, including after mistakes.
We change the plan during the match.

B.text: Builds pressure over several shots instead of going for winners too early.

A.text: Changes plan when the opponent adapts.

statements.text: I'm patient and wait for the right ball to attack.
I use several shots to set up a winner.
I change pace, height and direction to create openings.
I build pressure over several shots, instead of forcing it.

D.text: Stays calm in easy rallies, but gets frustrated after errors.

C.text: Stays calm in relaxed games. Tight scores bring rushed shots.

B.text: Usually calm at big points.

A.text: Plays the same whether ahead or behind.

statements.text: I stay calm in easy rallies.
I stay calm in friendly games, even after errors.
I stay calm at big points.
I don't rush my shots at tight scores.
I play the same whether we're ahead or behind.

C.text: Takes a few points to settle after a mistake.

B.text: Resets quickly after errors.

A.text: Treats errors as information and moves on right away.

statements.text: After a mistake, I'm over it within a few points.
I'm over it by the next point.
I use a routine to reset between points.
Mistakes don't change how I play.

D.text: Stays focused for short spells. Attention drifts after long rallies or lost points.

C.text: Focused for most of the match, with dips when tired.

statements.text: I stay focused in short spells.
I stay focused for most of the match.
I refocus quickly after a long rally or a lost point.

beginner.text: Gets the ball back over the net now and then. The walls are still confusing.

D.text: Gets most balls back over the net from the back, mostly cross-court. Little control of height or speed.

C.text: Keeps a steady rally from the back with a short swing. Aims low or to the middle.

B.text: Controls height, pace and direction. Hits to the feet, through the middle or down the line on purpose.

A.text: Uses slice, pace and angles to move opponents and set up the net. Rarely makes errors from the back.

statements.text: I can get the ball over the net from the back.
I keep a simple rally going from the back.
I use a short swing, not a big tennis swing.
I keep the ball low over the net.
I aim to the middle or a side on purpose.
I control height, pace and direction.
I can hit to the feet of net players when I need to.
I use slice, pace and angles to move opponents.
I rarely make errors from the back.

beginner.text: Not sure where to stand yet: back or net, left or right.

D.text: Knows the basic spots: both back or both at the net. Covers own side and doesn't get stuck in the middle of the court.

C.text: Moves forward and back with the play. Knows who covers the middle, and where to stand when serving and returning.

B.text: Adjusts position to the ball and the opponents, and covers for a partner who is pulled wide.

A.text: Reads opponents' habits and is already in position for the next ball.

statements.text: I know the basic spots: both back, or both at the net.
I cover my own side of the court.
I don't get stuck in the middle of the court.
I know where to stand when serving and returning.
I know who covers the middle.
I adjust my position to where the ball and opponents are.
I cover for my partner when they're pulled wide.
I'm already in position for the next ball.

D.text: Gets most easy volleys back over the net. Swings too much on fast balls.

C.text: Steady forehand and backhand volleys with a short swing. Aims deep or to the middle. Struggles with low and fast balls.

B.text: Controls low, high and fast volleys. Changes depth and pace on purpose: deep to push back, short or at the feet to finish.

A.text: Wins fast net exchanges. Uses block, drop and angled volleys to set up or finish, and rarely gives away an easy ball.

statements.text: I get most easy volleys back over the net.
I volley with a short, compact swing.
I can volley forehand and backhand with control.
I aim my volleys deep or to the middle.
I can control low volleys at my feet.
I handle fast balls at the net without panicking.
I change depth on purpose: deep to push back, short to finish.
I win most fast exchanges at the net.
I use angles and drop volleys to finish points.

C.text: Smashes short, easy lobs and keeps them in. Often hits too hard, and the ball comes back off the glass.

B.text: Picks the right lobs to smash. Places it to a corner or the feet, and gets back to the net after.

A.text: Smashes with control from most short lobs, using flat, kick and topspin to finish or push opponents back.

statements.text: I smash short, easy lobs and keep them in.
I don't smash every lob. I pick the short ones.
I place my smash to a corner or the feet.
I get back to the net after smashing.
I use flat, kick or topspin smashes on purpose.
My smash finishes points or pushes opponents well back.

B.text: Tries the x3 on very short lobs and gets it out about half the time.

A.text: Gets the x3 out over the side wall from short lobs in the middle, and knows when to try it and when not to.

statements.text: I try the x3 on very short lobs.
I get the x3 out over the side fence most times I try.
I know when the x3 is on, and when to play safe.

C.text: Gets some double glass balls back, often late or with little control.

B.text: Reads most double glass balls, waits for the ball and gets them back, often with a lob.

A.text: Handles double glass from both corners, and chooses a lob or a low ball depending on where opponents are.

statements.text: I get some double glass balls back.
I can tell which wall the ball will hit first.
I wait for the ball and get most double glass balls back, often with a lob.
I choose a lob or a low ball depending on where the opponents are.

C.text: Gets some smashes back when they come off the glass. Often gives up on hard ones.

B.text: Reads where a smash will bounce and gets most back, including off the back glass.

A.text: Gets back x3 and x4 smashes by running round or out of court where allowed, and turns some into counter-attacks.

statements.text: I get some smashes back when they come off the glass.
I read where a smash will bounce.
I get most smashes back, including off the back glass.
I chase x3 and x4 smashes where the court allows.
I turn some smash defences into counter-attacks.

C.text: Plays a soft, low ball to the net players' feet some of the time, then moves up.

B.text: Uses the chiquita on purpose to make opponents volley up, and moves up together with partner.

A.text: Disguises the chiquita and mixes it with lobs and passing shots so opponents can't predict it.

statements.text: I can play a soft, low ball to the net players' feet.
After a chiquita, I move up.
I use it on purpose to make opponents volley up.
My partner and I move up together after it.
I disguise it and mix it with lobs and passing shots.

C.text: Can block a fast ball back at the net, but it often sits up for the opponents.

B.text: Blocks fast balls low and deep with a short, firm racket.

A.text: Uses the block to change pace, landing it short or at the feet on purpose.

statements.text: I can block a fast ball back at the net.
My blocks land low or deep, not sitting up.
I use the block to change pace and land it at their feet.

B.text: Tries the drop volley when opponents are deep. It works some of the time.

A.text: Disguises the drop volley and uses it at the right moment to win the point.

statements.text: I try a drop volley when both opponents are deep.
My drop volley lands short and doesn't sit up.
I disguise it so opponents don't see it coming.

B.text: Can play a quick hook at the net on high balls, mostly to keep the ball in play.

A.text: Uses the hook to attack fast high balls at the net with control and placement.

statements.text: I can hit a quick hook on a high ball at the net.
I use the hook to attack, with control and placement.

A.text: Hits a topspin smash that kicks up off the back glass and pushes opponents back.

statements.text: I can hit a topspin smash that kicks up off the back glass.
I use it on purpose to push opponents back.

A.text: Can hit the x4 from very short balls near the net, and knows when it's on.

statements.text: I can hit an x4 out over the back on short, high balls.
I know when the x4 is on, and when to play safe.

B.text: Plays a drop shot when opponents are deep. Sometimes it sits up.

A.text: Disguises the drop shot and lands it short and low at the right moment.

statements.text: I play a drop shot when opponents are deep.
My drop shot lands short and low, not sitting up.
I disguise it and pick the right moment.

B.text: Can get the ball back with a back wall boast in emergencies.

A.text: Uses the back wall boast as a planned option when there's no other way forwards.

statements.text: In an emergency, I can hit the ball into my own back wall to get it over.
I use it as a planned option when there's no way to hit forwards.

C.text: Tries a lower, faster lob when opponents are very close to the net.

B.text: Uses the attacking lob on purpose to get behind net players and then moves up.

A.text: Disguises the attacking lob, so opponents can't move back early.

statements.text: I try a lower, faster lob when opponents are close to the net.
I use it on purpose to get behind net players.
I move up after it.
I disguise it so opponents can't move back early.

B.text: Hits a passing shot when there's an obvious gap. Often goes long or into the net.

A.text: Passes net players low down the line or through the middle on purpose.

statements.text: I hit a passing shot when there's a clear gap.
My passing shots stay low.
I pass net players down the line or through the middle on purpose.

C.text: Gets half volleys back when caught in the middle of the court, but they often pop up.

B.text: Keeps half volleys low and moves forward or back after them.

A.text: Uses the half volley to stay in a strong position, landing it low and deep.

statements.text: I get half volleys back when I'm caught in the middle.
My half volleys stay low.
After a half volley, I move forward or back, not stay in the middle.
I use the half volley to keep a strong position.
